[[Mangalore Electricity Supply Company Limited]] | successor = | founded = {{Start date and age|2005}} | founder = | hq_location_city = [[Mysore]], [[Karnataka]] | hq_location_country = India | num_locations = | num_locations_year = | areas_served = {{plainlist| * 27,858 square km. * [[Chamarajanagar district|Chamarajanagar]] * [[Hassan district|Hassan]] * [[Kodagu district|Kodagu]] * [[Mandya district|Mandya]] * [[Mysore district|Mysore]] }} | key_people = Chairman | products = | brands = | production = | production_year = | services = | revenue = {{Unbulleted list|{{increase}} {{INR}}2,991.06 [[crore]] (2015–16)|{{INR}}2,882.25 crore (2014–15)}} | operating_income = | income_year = | net_income = {{Unbulleted list|{{decrease}} {{INR}}7.92 crore (2015–16)|{{INR}}40.27 crore (2014–15)}} | assets = | assets_year = | equity = | equity_year = | owner = | num_members = | num_members_year = | num_employees = 5,066 | num_employees_year = March 2013 | parent = | divisions = | subsidiaries = | website = {{URL|cescmysore.org}} | footnotes = }} The '''Chamundeshwari Electricity Supply Corporation Limited''' ('''CESC''' '''Mysore''') is a company that provides electricity to five [[Districts of Karnataka|districts]] in the Indian [[States and union territories of India|State]] of [[Karnataka]]. It was carved out of [[Mangalore Electricity Supply Company Limited]] in 2005 and has its headquarters in [[Mysore]]. It is an [[State-owned enterprise|undertaking]] of the [[government of Karnataka]].{{cite web|title=Chamundeshwari Electricity Supply Corporation Limited Profile|url=http://knowledgeplatform.in/wp-content/uploads/2016/01/Chamundeshwari-Electricity-Supply_1st-Prize.pdf|publisher=knowledgeplatform.in|access-date=7 March 2017}} == History == Electricity was distributed in the five districts of [[Chamarajanagar district|Chamarajanagar]], [[Hassan district|Hassan]], [[Kodagu district|Kodagu]], [[Mandya district|Mandya]], [[Mysore district|Mysore]] by [[Karnataka Power Transmission Corporation]] (KPTCL) since its formation in 1999 to 2002. [[Mangalore Electricity Supply Company Limited]] (MESCOM) was one of four companies that was formed in 2002 from KPTCL, and it distributed to these districts. CESC was carved out of MESCOM in 2005 to meet the increasing demand for power.{{cite magazine|last=Sharma|first=Ravi|date=16–29 February 2008|title=Business of power|url=http://www.frontline.in/static/html/fl2504/stories/20080229506110700.htm|magazine=[[Frontline (magazine)|Frontline]]|access-date=7 March 2017}} Kodagu was added to its jurisdiction in 2006.{{cite web|title=11th Annual Accounts for the Year 2015-16|url=http://www.cescmysore.org/images/Annualreport/WD-137-CESCOM-Eng-Print.pdf|work=Chamundeshwari Electricity Supply Corporation|accessdate=7 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170308044415/http://www.cescmysore.org/images/Annualreport/WD-137-CESCOM-Eng-Print.pdf|archive-date=8 March 2017|url-status=dead}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== {{Portal|Energy|Companies}} * {{Official website|www.cescmysore.org}} {{Power Plants of Karnataka}} {{Authority control}} [[Category:Companies based in Karnataka]] [[Category:Electric power distribution network operators in India]] [[Category:State agencies of Karnataka]] [[Category:State electricity agencies of India]] [[Category:Energy in Karnataka]] [[Category:Indian companies established in 2005]] [[Category:2005 establishments in Karnataka]] {{Energy-company-stub}}
extract: The Chamundeshwari Electricity Supply Corporation Limited (CESC Mysore) is a company that provides electricity to five districts in the Indian State of Karnataka. It was carved out of Mangalore Electricity Supply Company Limited in 2005 and has its headquarters in Mysore. It is an undertaking of the government of Karnataka.
